body_en_plain:
July, 1996  No.107  Page Reply


 How to write to us...02     -
 Alan D. Cox..........03     -
 R. Webster...........05    07
 Michael Atkins.......11    12
 John White...........13    18
 Francis Miles........23     -
 Dave Knott...........25    27
 Graham Yeardley......33    35

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From Alan D. Cox, ST. CLEARS





Dear Brian,


Many of your subscribers will
have started their computing
experience with one or the other
of Sir Clive Sinclair's products
- the ZX80, ZX81, etc, etc. They
therefore may be interested to
know that Enrico Tedeschi, cura-
tor of the International Elect-
ronics Museum in Brighton, has
published a book about Uncle
Clive's achievements called
'Sinclair Archaeology'...


To quote from the leaflet, 'In
particular you will find - an
illustration of every Sinclair
product ever made - a complete
list of Sinclair products in
chronological order - technical
details and assembling instruct-
ions for many Sinclair products
- advertisement reproductions
from the magazines of the time -
inside information on Sinclair
history:a complete bibliography.

If anyone is interested - and
no, I am not on a commission -
the book is available for `10
plus `2 p&p from Enricho
Tedeschi, 54 Easthill Drive,
Portslade, Brighton, BN41 2FD,
United Kingdom.
                        Alan

From: R. Webster, WILLENHALL

Could you say if I could still
get hold of the Oct 1988 issue
of OUTLET with the BASIC TRACE
on it. I do have one with BETA
BASIC but it tends to crash with
some programs. What I need is
one that will trace any program
straight off.

The other is Issue 45 that has
the telephone codes in it. Now,
as my computer system is in
Australia and I am using a 128+2
black case computer while I am
at the above address, if I get
the 3.5" disks for my Plus D
(that is in Australia), could
you put the telephone codes and
the Trace on a tape so that I
could look at them while here!

The next question is - will the
Plus D interface from Datel that
I have on my Spectrum 48K Plus
(in Auss) connect to this 128+2A
and be OK?

Could you please say what the
cost would be? Most grateful.


                  R. Webster

Ron Cavers to R. Webster


I can't find a Basic Trace in
Issue No.14 - I think you must
mean Issue No.38 which was Oct
1990, not the Oct 1998 issue.

Whether it will run with any
Basic program depends - you do
need some space for the machine
code (although that is relocat-
able) - but it worked on all
that we tested it with at the
time.

Issue No.45 is available - as
are all back issues of OUTLET -
but remember that the STD Codes
are MASTERFILE files so you will
need that program to use them.


When we discontinued the tape
version of OUTLET it co-incided
with two other events - our main
cassette recorder finally gave
up the ghost and our stocks of
blank tapes ran out. Obviously,
we still have tape recorders but
these prove to be a confounded
nuisance every time we have to
use them (fortunately, rarely).
For instance, when we get the
odd program in on tape, we often
have have to try two or three
recorders and make several
attempts to load the files to
transfer them to disk. And to do
the reverse is really hard work,
to pick out an odd program from
a tape master and copy it to
another tape is a non-starter -
it would be cheaper to buy the
issue as it stood (if we had it)

Probably the easiest option for
us would be to copy the relative
files from the disk master onto
a tape but then you would need
to be aware that it would be the
disk version - which can differ
quite a bit from the tape vers-
ion so you might need to tinker
with it to get it to run proper-
ly. Again, the cost might be a
barrier as we'd need to charge
the full issue cost. Now, on to
the Plus D interface. The short
answer is no, you cannot connect
the interface you have to the
128K+2A.There are slight differ-
ences in the hardware so you
would need the "widget" which is
provided by Datel, when you buy
the Plus D interface, according
to which version of the Spectrum
you have.

I imagine Datel will sell these
separately and I am sending you
their leaflet so that you can
contact them if you wish.

                        Ron

From: Michael Atkins, BURY

Dear Ron & Brian,

I finally got round to reading
OUTLET after a year in which
work interfered with my leisure
time. I noticed John Cleveland
was asking if there is an update
of the database which appeared
in OUTLET 78. The answer to this
is that there is - but only up
to March, 1995 - so I will make
it my first +3 task to bring it
right up to date!

        Yours sincerely,

        Michael Atkins

Brian Cavers to Michael Atkins

Many thanks, Michael and we look
forward to publishing the update
in a future issue.

                     Brian

From: John H.B. White, LEICESTER

Dear Ron & Brian,

Thanks for the continuing high
quality of your magazine.

You may remember that I am one
of those who convert OUTLET for
my faithful old Opus interface
and I am therefore unable to
send this on a +D or Disciple
disc; hence the paper.

Thank you for continuing to
include lines 9980, etc. in your
BASIC listings and also for the
occasional Opus/Microdrive type
LOAD/SAVE/PRINT lines that still
remain in other places in prog-
rams.


On the subject of the Opus, I
understand that it needs some of
the Spectrum RAM in order to
function. Some years ago I found
in a magazine a method of trans-
ferring programs with long mach-
ine codes from tape to Opus and
was able to do this for SCRABBLE
which sets RAMTOP to 24000. The
Opus cannot manage this because
it needs some of the Spectrum
RAM in order to operate. I think
the method was to clear to 25000
and send the first 1K to the
screen, later moving it to the
right place when the Opus had
finished [disk operations].

Would this explain why I cannot
load some of the large demos
whose machine code files start
as low as the 24000's?

An example of one which I can't
load is LYRA2 in Issue 105.
Perhaps the +D/Disciple doesn't
need the Spectrum RAM. Can any-
one help with an explanation
either direct to the address
above or to OUTLET, in case oth-
ers have this problem?

I was interested in the letter
from George B.Munro in Issue 103
increasing the number of lives
in the patience game NAPOLEON
(Issue 102) as I was thinking
along the same lines,having also
found the game almost imposs-
ible. Before I explain, may I
point out what may be an error
in the program?when the demo has
been run we are invited to press
a key to go to the menu.However,


we go back and get the demo
again, being stuck in an endless
loop! I found that if BASIC line
1290 is changed to RUN instead
of GO TO 90, all is well.

Back to lives; my method adds
"bells and whistles" by offering
the player either the standard 3
lives or a choice of 1 to 9,this
being selected before starting.
Thus you are stuck with your
choice! The current round number
and selected number of lives
appear at the bottom of the
screen as, for example, R2/5 for
Round 2 out of 5.

Several lines are added to the
BASIC; some are new while others
replace the original lines.


[The added lines are saved on
this OUTLET disk as "NAPMERGE"
and can be MERGEd into NAPOLEON
by first loading NAPOLEON,press-
ing BREAK and entering...
MERGE "NAPMERGE" (use the syntax
appropriate to your system). To
make this permanent you need to
resave the program with RUN 9972
(+3), 9982 (+D) or 9983 (tape).
I recommend you do this on a
separate disc or tape from your
OUTLET issue. Note that lines
2040, 2320, 3010 and 3020 now
have a REM at the start so they
are inoperative but not lost -
Brian]

This letter is probably too long
so I will shut up and send my
best wishes to all at OUTLET.
                     John White


Brian Cavers to John White

I believe you take the +D OUTLET
and convert it to Opus but I do
not recollect whether you have a
+D or use software on the Opus
to convert the files - I think
the latter. If you had a +D you
could make a snapshot of a demo
and then use SNAPDRAGON in last
month's OUTLET to produce code
files. These work in much the
same way as you described - by
loading the bottom part of the
code into the screen and then
copying it to low memory at the
last moment after disk loading
has ended. Apart from that you
would need a customised version
of every file that loads too low
for the Opus.


At its simplest you need a tiny
machine code routine to copy the
code part to 24000 and then jump
to the start address. Suppose a
code file is CODE 24000,35000.If
you load it to say 26000 and
then save it again in two parts
as 26000,1000 and 27000,34000 it
then needs a bit of code at the
start or end of the first part..

LD HL, 16384 ;top of screen
LD DE, 24000 ;destination
LD BC, 1000  ;length
LDIR         ;copy to 24000
JP nn        ;nn=USR address

If you load that to 17384 and
the first bit of code to 16384
and save it as 16384,1015 then
to load and run it use...


LOAD "PART1.C" CODE 16384
LOAD "PART2.C" CODE 25000
RANDOMIZE USR 17384

The code could be compiled and
POKEd from BASIC with...

LET A=17384 : RESTORE
FOR N=1 TO 5
READ B,C
LET HI=INT(C/256)
LET LO=C-HI*256
POKE A,B  : LET A=A+1
POKE A,LO : LET A=A+1
POKE A,HI : LET A=A+1
NEXT N
DATA 33,16384,17,24000,1,1000
DATA 237,176,195,nn

LOAD "PART1.C" CODE 16384
SAVE "PART1.C" CODE 16384,1015


Replace the nn with the USR add-
ress from the original listing.
You may also need to put in an
ERASE "PART1.C" between the LOAD
and SAVE - I just forget whether
the Opus will crash if it tries
to save and the filename already
exists.

Note that the code goes into the
screen memory so if you get an
error while saving (say you for-
get to put a disk in), DON'T re-
RUN from the LOAD or SAVE lines
or clear the screen - re-RUN it
from the start!

Once saved you load Part 1 and
Part 2 and then RANDOMIZE USR
17384 to copy the code from the
screen to 24000 and run it.


This may not work with all files
because some load code into 128K
page memory or set up the screen
in a certain way and will crash
if it is corrupted with code but
it is worth exploring. Let me
know if you need more help.

That error in Napoleon sounds
like our fault not the original
author's. I have typed your new
lines in to save everyone else
doing it. I've double-checked it
but keep your fingers crossed I
haven't mistyped anything!

                          Brian

From Francis Miles, WELWYN


Here's a puzzle: if you have a
cube made of wood, and saw it
into two pieces, obviously the
cut face will be a polygon
(with straight sides).

1. How many different kinds of
polygon (ie different numbers of
sides) can be made by making
this single cut in different
directions?

2. Obviously, by cutting paral-
lel to one face you can make a
'regular' quadrilateral, ie one
with all its sides and angles
equal, a square. What other
regular polygons can you make?


I'll give the answers next
month. I find that when I can't
sleep at night, thinking about
things like this knocks me out
quite quickly(anything non-verb-
al and non-numerical will do
it). Until recently, I've always
dropped off just when the solu-
tions were coming in sight; but
I think I've got it all now.

         Francis Miles

From:     D. Knott
      8 Earls Barton Road
          Mears Ashby
          Northampton
            NN6 0DR
          01604-812108




Dear Ron or Brian,

If anyone has or had an Amstrad
DMP-2000 printer, and still has
the instruction manual, I would
be obliged if you could write or
telephone [ABOVE ADDRESS] as I
need to know what the DIP switch
settings are/can be and also the
control codes to change the
print styles and formats.


I am able to reimburse postage
or return the manual as soon as
I have copied the required inf-
ormation that I am desperate to
know....somebody..please help as
soon as possible...thanks very
much.

Also does anyone have Masterfile
+3 instructions as I've got a
duff Tasword 3 file here and I
need to know how to use the Conv
program and the subsequent
Import for old Masterfile files
to Masterfile 3 files.

Thanks again for a very enter-
taining Disczine.

             Dave


Brian Cavers to David Knott





I don't have the Amstrad DMP2000
manual but have put that part of
your letter in our OUTBOARD area
and, because it is a popular
printer, hopefully someone will
contact you with the information
you want.

The full Masterfile +3 instruct-
ions together with Masterfile +3
itself were in OUTLET 76 (but in
the +3 version only).I reproduce
the section on converting old
48K Masterfile files starting on
the next page...


 48K MF FILE CONVERSION TO MF +3
 -------------------------------
The original Spectrum MASTERFILE
(version 01 to 09) saved its
files as character arrays, and
has no export option.Such arrays
are not suitable for direct
import into MF+3, so we have
provided a utility called CONV
which will process these files
and produce ASCII data files
which can then be imported into
MF+3. The conversion of an old
Spectrum MF file is as follows :

a) Save the file only to disk
from Masterfile 48K. If you can
only save to tape you can copy
from tape to +3 disc with...

 LOAD"T:filename" DATA f$():
 SAVE"A:filename" DATA f$()

b)Use program CONV to generate
an ASCII file from this.

c)Import the ASCII file into
MASTERFILE +3

The program CONV asks for input
and output file names and a list
of data references. The order of
this list determines the order
of data in each output record.
Enter the data references one
after the other with no opening
quotes, no spaces or commas, and
end the list with [ENTER].

Any data reference not found
creates a null item on the ASCII
file.You can make use of this if
a new file has data names which
do not correspond with the old


file, by just keying a "." for
absent references, eg,if the old
file has references N,A,T but a
new file needs these fields as
1st, 2nd, and 6th fields, give a
list of: NA...T

Any line-break characters found
in the data will be converted
from "I" to "-".

On completion, the record count
is shown and another file
conversion is prompted. To end,
just reset the machine. Data
names and display formats are
not transferable.

The whole character array F$
file is read in before the
output file name is solicited,


giving you the chance to change
discs for the output file. The
input file is validated and any
file which does not look like a
old MASTERFILE file is not
accepted.


To transfer the output of CONV
into an MF+3 file, first use
MF+3 to initialise a new file
with suitable structure, or load
an existing file. Take care that
the data names correspond with
the data references specified to
CONV. Then use the IMPORT funct-
ion of MF+3. Reply [N] to each
of the questions about quote
wrap, comma-delimiters, and re-
cord separators.



Once you have successfully imp-
orted the CONV output and saved
the resulting MF+3 file there is
no need to keep the intermediate
file.

                       Brian

From: Graham Yeardley, CAMBRIDGE




Dear Ron & Brian,


I followed Cristian Secara's
advice in Outlet 85 or 86 about
copying Tasword 3 to a DS, DD
3.5" B:drive for a Plus 3
Spectrum and it works fine. My
version is 2.O6 dated O4O489.

I also put the dictionary file
onto the same disc. The check
word function works but the
fuller check text needs the disc
in drive A to work as does the
customise option.


Regarding the review that app-
eared in the last issue regard-
ing D Morris's DiscDos (which I
have ordered), will it allow +3
users to take the +D version
when 3" discs dry up?

              Regards,

              Graham Yeardley.

Brian Cavers to Graham Yeardley

Yes, as John Cleveland reported
in his review, he ran the +D
OUTLET 103 successfully on his
+3 B drive using DiscDos with no
problems. There may be the odd
program that does not work but
in general it is a good emulator
of the +D. Note that John does
mention that after installation,
RAMTOP is left at 31999 so you
need to raise this to 65367 with
a CLEAR 65367. I assume you can
this to the installation BASIC
to make it automatic.

We are considering getting the
full DISCDOS ourselves when we
can get a 3.5" drive sorted out.
                      Brian.

From: R. Webster, WILLENHALL

Could you say if I could still get hold of the Oct 1988 issue of OUTLET with the BASIC TRACE on it. I do have one with BETA BASIC but it tends to crash with some programs. What I need is one that will trace any program straight off.

The other is Issue 45 that has the telephone codes in it. Now, as my computer system is in Australia and I am using a 128+2 black case computer while I am at the above address, if I get the 3.5" disks for my Plus D (that is in Australia), could you put the telephone codes and the Trace on a tape so that I could look at them while here!

The next question is - will the Plus D interface from Datel that I have on my Spectrum 48K Plus (in Auss) connect to this 128+2A and be OK?

Could you please say what the cost would be? Most grateful.

R. Webster

Ron Cavers to R. Webster

I can't find a Basic Trace in Issue No.14 - I think you must mean Issue No.38 which was Oct 1990, not the Oct 1998 issue.

Whether it will run with any Basic program depends - you do need some space for the machine code (although that is relocat- able) - but it worked on all that we tested it with at the time.

Issue No.45 is available - as are all back issues of OUTLET - but remember that the STD Codes are MASTERFILE files so you will need that program to use them.

When we discontinued the tape version of OUTLET it co-incided with two other events - our main cassette recorder finally gave up the ghost and our stocks of blank tapes ran out. Obviously, we still have tape recorders but these prove to be a confounded nuisance every time we have to use them (fortunately, rarely). For instance, when we get the odd program in on tape, we often have have to try two or three recorders and make several attempts to load the files to transfer them to disk. And to do the reverse is really hard work, to pick out an odd program from a tape master and copy it to another tape is a non-starter - it would be cheaper to buy the issue as it stood (if we had it)

Probably the easiest option for us would be to copy the relative files from the disk master onto a tape but then you would need to be aware that it would be the disk version - which can differ quite a bit from the tape vers- ion so you might need to tinker with it to get it to run proper- ly. Again, the cost might be a barrier as we'd need to charge the full issue cost. Now, on to the Plus D interface. The short answer is no, you cannot connect the interface you have to the 128K+2A.There are slight differ- ences in the hardware so you would need the "widget" which is provided by Datel, when you buy the Plus D interface, according to which version of the Spectrum you have.

I imagine Datel will sell these separately and I am sending you their leaflet so that you can contact them if you wish.

```text
                        Ron
```

48K MF FILE CONVERSION TO MF +3

The original Spectrum MASTERFILE (version 01 to 09) saved its files as character arrays, and has no export option.Such arrays are not suitable for direct import into MF+3, so we have provided a utility called CONV which will process these files and produce ASCII data files which can then be imported into MF+3. The conversion of an old Spectrum MF file is as follows :

a) Save the file only to disk from Masterfile 48K. If you can only save to tape you can copy from tape to +3 disc with...

LOAD"T:filename" DATA f$(): SAVE"A:filename" DATA f$()

b)Use program CONV to generate an ASCII file from this.

c)Import the ASCII file into MASTERFILE +3

The program CONV asks for input and output file names and a list of data references. The order of this list determines the order of data in each output record. Enter the data references one after the other with no opening quotes, no spaces or commas, and end the list with [ENTER].

Any data reference not found creates a null item on the ASCII file.You can make use of this if a new file has data names which do not correspond with the old

file, by just keying a "." for absent references, eg,if the old file has references N,A,T but a new file needs these fields as 1st, 2nd, and 6th fields, give a list of: NA...T

Any line-break characters found in the data will be converted from "I" to "-".

On completion, the record count is shown and another file conversion is prompted. To end, just reset the machine. Data names and display formats are not transferable.

The whole character array F$ file is read in before the output file name is solicited,

giving you the chance to change discs for the output file. The input file is validated and any file which does not look like a old MASTERFILE file is not accepted.

To transfer the output of CONV into an MF+3 file, first use MF+3 to initialise a new file with suitable structure, or load an existing file. Take care that the data names correspond with the data references specified to CONV. Then use the IMPORT funct- ion of MF+3. Reply [N] to each of the questions about quote wrap, comma-delimiters, and re- cord separators.

Once you have successfully imp- orted the CONV output and saved the resulting MF+3 file there is no need to keep the intermediate file.

Brian

### Ron Cavers отвечает R. Webster

Я не могу найти Basic Trace в выпуске №14 — думаю, вы имели в виду выпуск №38 за октябрь 1990 года, а не октябрь 1988-го.

Будет ли он работать с любой программой на Бейсике — это зависит от обстоятельств: вам потребуется немного места для машинного кода (хотя он и перемещаемый) — но он работал на всем, на чем мы его тогда тестировали.

Выпуск №45 доступен — как и все старые номера OUTLET, — но помните, что файлы STD Codes являются файлами MASTERFILE, поэтому для их использования вам понадобится эта программа.

Когда мы прекратили выпуск кассетной версии OUTLET, это совпало с двумя другими событиями — наш основной магнитофон окончательно испустил дух, а запасы чистых кассет подошли к концу. Разумеется, магнитофоны у нас все еще есть, но каждый раз, когда нам приходится ими пользоваться (к счастью, редко), это оказывается сущей мукой. Например, когда нам присылают редкую программу на кассете, нам часто приходится перебирать два или три магнитофона и делать несколько попыток загрузить файлы, чтобы перенести их на диск. А делать обратное — поистине тяжкий труд: выцепить отдельную программу с мастер-кассеты и скопировать ее на другую кассету совершенно нереально — проще было бы купить номер целиком, как он есть (если бы он у нас был).

Вероятно, самым простым вариантом для нас было бы скопировать нужные файлы с мастер-диска на кассету, но тогда вам нужно иметь в виду, что это будет дисковая версия, которая может довольно сильно отличаться от кассетной, так что вам, возможно, придется повозиться с ней, чтобы заставить ее работать как следует. Опять же, препятствием может стать цена, так как нам придется взять полную стоимость номера.

Теперь о Plus D интерфейсе. Короткий ответ — нет, вы не можете подключить имеющийся у вас интерфейс к 128K+2A. В «железе» есть небольшие различия, поэтому вам понадобится специальный переходник («widget»), который поставляется Datel при покупке интерфейса Plus D в зависимости от того, какая у вас версия Spectrum.

Я предполагаю, что Datel продает их отдельно, и я высылаю вам их буклет, чтобы вы могли связаться с ними, если пожелаете.

Ron

### Brian Cavers отвечает John White

Если не ошибаюсь, вы берете версию OUTLET для +D и конвертируете ее для Opus, но я не помню, есть ли у вас +D или вы используете софт на Opus для конвертации файлов — думаю, последнее. Если бы у вас был +D, вы могли бы сделать снимок (snapshot) демоверсии, а затем использовать SNAPDRAGON из прошлого номера OUTLET, чтобы получить файлы кодов. Они работают примерно так же, как вы описали — загружая нижнюю часть кода в экранную память, а затем в последний момент, после завершения загрузки с диска, копируя ее в младшую память. Кроме того, вам понадобится модифицированная версия каждого файла, который загружается слишком низко для Opus.

В простейшем случае вам потребуется крошечная подпрограмма в машинных кодах, чтобы скопировать часть кода в 24000, а затем перейти по адресу запуска. Предположим, файл кодов — это CODE 24000,35000. Если вы загрузите его, скажем, в 26000, а затем сохраните снова в двух частях как 26000,1000 и 27000,34000, то в начале или конце первой части потребуется небольшой кусочек кода:

```text
LD HL, 16384 ;начало экрана
LD DE, 24000 ;назначение
LD BC, 1000  ;длина
LDIR         ;копировать в 24000
JP nn        ;nn=адрес USR
```

Если вы загрузите его в 17384, а первую часть кода — в 16384, и сохраните это как 16384,1015, то для загрузки и запуска используйте:

```text
LOAD "PART1.C" CODE 16384
LOAD "PART2.C" CODE 25000
RANDOMIZE USR 17384
```

Код можно скомпилировать и записать с помощью POKE из Бейсика:

```text
LET A=17384 : RESTORE
FOR N=1 TO 5
READ B,C
LET HI=INT(C/256)
LET LO=C-HI*256
POKE A,B  : LET A=A+1
POKE A,LO : LET A=A+1
POKE A,HI : LET A=A+1
NEXT N
DATA 33,16384,17,24000,1,1000
DATA 237,176,195,nn

LOAD "PART1.C" CODE 16384
SAVE "PART1.C" CODE 16384,1015
```

Замените nn на адрес USR из исходного листинга. Возможно, вам также придется вставить ERASE "PART1.C" между LOAD и SAVE — я точно не помню, зависает ли Opus при попытке сохранения, если файл с таким именем уже существует.

Обратите внимание, что код помещается в память экрана, поэтому, если вы получите ошибку во время сохранения (скажем, забудете вставить диск), НЕ перезапускайте программу со строк LOAD или SAVE и не очищайте экран — перезапустите ее с самого начала!

После сохранения вы загружаете Part 1 и Part 2, а затем выполняете RANDOMIZE USR 17384, чтобы скопировать код из экрана в 24000 и запустить его.

Это может сработать не со всеми файлами, так как некоторые загружают код в страницы памяти 128K или настраивают экран определенным образом и будут сбоить, если он окажется поврежден кодом, но попробовать стоит. Дайте знать, если вам понадобится дополнительная помощь.

Эта ошибка в Napoleon, похоже, наша вина, а не первоначального автора. Я набрал ваши новые строки, чтобы избавить всех остальных от этой работы. Я все перепроверил, но держите кулачки, чтобы я нигде не опечатался!

Brian

### Brian Cavers отвечает David Knott

У меня нет руководства к Amstrad DMP2000, но я поместил эту часть вашего письма в наш раздел OUTBOARD, и, поскольку это популярный принтер, будем надеяться, что кто-нибудь свяжется с вами и предоставит нужную информацию.

Полная инструкция к Masterfile +3 вместе с самим Masterfile +3 была в OUTLET 76 (но только в версии для +3). Я привожу раздел по конвертации старых файлов Masterfile от 48K со следующей страницы...

```text
 48K MF FILE CONVERSION TO MF +3
 -------------------------------
```

Оригинальный MASTERFILE для Spectrum (версии от 01 до 09) сохранял файлы в виде символьных массивов и не имел функции экспорта. Такие массивы не подходят для прямого импорта в MF+3, поэтому мы предоставили утилиту под названием CONV, которая обрабатывает эти файлы и создает файлы данных ASCII, которые затем можно импортировать в MF+3. Конвертация старого файла MF для Spectrum выглядит следующим образом:

a) Сохраните файл только на диск из Masterfile 48K. Если вы можете сохранять только на кассету, скопировать с кассеты на диск +3 можно с помощью:

```text
LOAD "T:filename" DATA f$():
SAVE "A:filename" DATA f$()
```

b) С помощью программы CONV создайте из него ASCII-файл.

c) Импортируйте ASCII-файл в MASTERFILE +3.

Программа CONV запрашивает имена входного и выходного файлов, а также список ссылок на данные (data references). Порядок этого списка определяет порядок данных в каждой выходной записи. Вводите ссылки на данные друг за другом без открывающих кавычек, без пробелов или запятых, а в конце списка нажмите [ENTER].

Любая ненайденная ссылка на данные создает пустой элемент в ASCII-файле. Вы можете использовать это, если в новом файле имена данных не соответствуют старому файлу, просто набрав «.» для отсутствующих ссылок. Например, если в старом файле есть ссылки N, A, T, а в новом файле эти поля должны быть 1-м, 2-м и 6-м полями, задайте список: NA...T.

Любые символы переноса строки, обнаруженные в данных, будут преобразованы из «I» в «-».

По завершении отображается количество записей и предлагается конвертировать следующий файл. Чтобы выйти, просто перезагрузите компьютер. Имена данных и форматы отображения не переносятся.

Весь файл символьного массива F$ считывается до того, как будет запрошено имя выходного файла, что дает вам возможность сменить диски для записи выходного файла. Входной файл проходит проверку, и любой файл, не похожий на старый файл MASTERFILE, не принимается.

Чтобы перенести результат работы CONV в файл MF+3, сначала используйте MF+3 для инициализации нового файла с подходящей структурой или загрузите существующий файл. Убедитесь, что имена данных соответствуют ссылкам на данные, указанным в CONV. Затем воспользуйтесь функцией IMPORT в MF+3. Отвечайте [N] на каждый из вопросов об обрамлении кавычками (quote wrap), разделителях-запятых (comma-delimiters) и разделителях записей (record separators).

После того как вы успешно импортировали результат CONV и сохранили получившийся файл MF+3, промежуточный файл хранить нет необходимости.

Brian

### Brian Cavers отвечает Graham Yeardley

Да, как сообщил John Cleveland в своем обзоре, он без проблем успешно запустил +D-версию OUTLET 103 на своем дисководе B: компьютера +3 с помощью DiscDos. Возможно, попадутся отдельные неработающие программы, но в целом это хороший эмулятор +D. Обратите внимание: John упоминает, что после установки RAMTOP остается на уровне 31999, поэтому вам нужно поднять его до 65367 с помощью CLEAR 65367. Полагаю, вы можете добавить это в установочный Бейсик, чтобы процесс происходил автоматически.

Мы и сами подумываем приобрести полную версию DISCDOS, как только разберемся с дисководом 3.5".

Brian.
